---
title: Authoring schemas
description: "Declaring a new element type in a moddle YAML schema, and how its fields reach the inspector."
---

Schema definitions are direct moddle YAML, shipped from `assets/schemas/`. Four are **core** (`core: true` — always loaded, never disabled from the settings); the rest are domain extensions a user switches on.

| File | Prefix | What it declares |
|---|---|---|
| `studyflow.moddle.yaml` | `studyflow` | The core language: `Study`, `StartEvent`, `EndEvent`, `SequenceFlow`, the `BaseElement`/`Scheduling`/`Classification` traits, and the data-infrastructure types (`Schema`, `Dataset`, `DataCatalog`, `Table`, `Timeseries`, `EventMarker`). It also declares the inspector's shared tabs. **core** |
| `prov.moddle.yaml` | `prov` | `Activity` — one entry of the provenance trail (who did what, with which tool, when). **core** |
| `functional.moddle.yaml` | `functional` | `Transform`, `Map`, `Reduce`, `Filter` — the generic verbs domain layers root their presets on. **core** |
| `cognitive.moddle.yaml` | `cognitive` | `CognitiveTask`, `Rest`, `Questionnaire`, `Instruction`, `BehaverseTask`, `RandomGateway`, `EligibilityGateway`, `Actor`. Split out of the core so adopters can swap the cognitive layer. **core** |
| `agentic.moddle.yaml` | `agentic` | LLM and agent workflows: `Agent`, `Router`, `LLMCall`, `Tool`, `HumanApproval`, `Prompt`, `Memory`. Nothing in this set executes. |
| `ml.moddle.yaml` | `ml` | scikit-learn pipeline presets. Templates only — it declares no types. |
| `eeg.moddle.yaml` | `eeg` | `Session` and `Recording` for biosignal acquisition, plus the EEGPrep/fMRIPrep presets. |

## The file header

```yaml
name: Core
prefix: studyflow
description: Core BPMN extension for modeling research processes.
uri: http://behaverse.org/schemas/studyflow/v1   # version segment = studyflow format version
icon: iconify tabler--hexagon-letter-s   # optional, shown in the modeler
core: true          # optional: always loaded, cannot be disabled
order: 10           # registry position (load precedence + settings order)
version: 26.0716
xml:
  tagAlias: lowerCase
categories: []      # inspector tabs; the core schema declares the shared ones
enumerations: []
types: []
templates: []
```

| Key | Rule |
|---|---|
| `uri` | Required and validated at load. A file missing it, or reusing a `prefix` another file already claims, is rejected by name rather than silently producing an unnamespaced or half-overwritten schema. There is no namespace migration mechanism: a bump is a breaking change to saved files, not something a header can absorb. |
| `prefix` | Appears in every saved file, and need not match `name` — the core schema is named `Core` and prefixed `studyflow`. |
| `description` | Renders in a tooltip in the schema palette, so keep it to a sentence or two. |
| `icon` | Optional, a URL or `iconify <name>`, shown next to the schema name. |
| `order` | Registry position: load precedence, and order in the settings. |

## Inspector tabs (`categories`)

A property names its tab in `meta.categories`. The core schema declares the shared tabs — `General` · `Documentation` · `Gantt` · `Data` · `Execution` — and other schemas file into them or add one, as `cognitive` adds `Behaverse`. A category no schema declares still works, but sorts last. `Execution` is `synthetic: true`: a section component draws it over nested BPMN state (properties, data associations, loop characteristics), so it appears even with no attributes filed under it.

## Enumerations

`enumerations` are reusable closed value lists, referenced from a property's `type:`.

```yaml
enumerations:
  - name: CompletionCodeTypeEnum
    isAbstract: true
    description: How the completion code is generated when the study ends.
    literalValues:
      - name: None
        value: none
        description: No completion code is issued.
      - name: Static
        value: static
      - name: Dynamic
        value: dynamic
```

## Types and properties

Two relationships compose a type.

| Relationship | Use it to | And then |
|---|---|---|
| `extends` | Add attributes to an existing BPMN class without creating a new visual element — extending `bpmn:StartEvent` with `consentFormUri`, say. | With `isAbstract: true` it is a **trait**: never placed on the canvas, only contributing attributes to whatever it names. |
| `superClass` | Define a new concrete element. | List the BPMN base first (`bpmn:Task`, `bpmn:ExclusiveGateway`, `bpmn:DataStoreReference`) and add `bpmn:BaseElement` so the inspector picks up the standard metadata fields. Pair it with `meta.bpmnType` so the modeler knows which BPMN shape to render. |

```yaml
types:
  - name: StartEvent
    extends:
      - bpmn:StartEvent
    isAbstract: true
    properties:
      - name: consentFormUri
        description: Link to the consent form. Untick to skip the consent step.
        isAttr: true
        type: String
        meta:
          optional: true
          categories:
            - General

  - name: RandomGateway
    description: Assigns participants to an outgoing branch at random.
    superClass:
      - bpmn:ExclusiveGateway
      - bpmn:BaseElement
    meta:
      icon: iconify streamline-flex--dice-5
      bpmnType: bpmn:ExclusiveGateway
    properties:
      - name: algorithm
        isAttr: true
        type: studyflow:AssignmentAlgorithmEnum
        default: probabilistic
        meta:
          categories:
            - General
```

### Redefining a BPMN attribute

bpmn-moddle already carries every BPMN attribute, and the inspector shows **none** of them: a field renders only when a schema declares it. `redefines` makes a native attribute editable, so a schema's `redefines` list is this layer's list of which BPMN attributes a studyflow author edits — delete the trait below and the field disappears while the attribute stays in the file.

```yaml
- name: Implementation
  extends:
    - bpmn:ServiceTask
  isAbstract: true
  properties:
    - name: bpmn:implementation
      description: Software this step runs, as `<scheme>://<ref>[@<version>]`.
      isAttr: true
      type: String
      redefines: bpmn:ServiceTask#implementation
```

### Property modifiers

| Key | Effect |
|---|---|
| `isAttr: true` | Serialized as an XML attribute in the BPMN XML form (most scalar properties). The YAML `.studyflow` format maps every property to a plain key regardless. |
| `isBody: true` | Serialized as the element's text body in the BPMN XML form. Used for free-form content like YAML `configurations`. |
| `isMany: true` | Repeated property, rendered as a list in the inspector. |
| `default` | Initial value. |
| `redefines` | Override the type, default, or visibility of an inherited property (above). |
| `replaces` | Replace an inherited property entirely. |
| `xml.serialize: property` / `xsi:type` | How a complex-typed property is written. Needed when redefining BPMN's own expression elements, which are named after the property rather than the type. |

| `meta` key on a property | Effect |
|---|---|
| `categories: [Data]` | The tab the property lives under. |
| `order: 1` | Position within its tab; unordered properties sort after ordered ones. |
| `pinned: true` | Always visible, even when the value is empty. |
| `optional: true` | The inspector shows a checkbox to opt the property in. |
| `editable: true` | An enum property also accepts free-text entries. |
| `editor: code` | Which input component edits it (`code`, `markdown`, `csvw-table`). A value *type* may name one for all its properties instead, which is how every `studyflow:YAMLString` gets the code editor. |
| `readonly: true` | Display-only; written by the runner, not by hand. |
| `legacyNames: [category]` | Earlier spellings, still read from old files and rewritten on save. |
| `condition.language: json` + `condition.body: { otherField: value }` | Visibility predicate: the property appears only when other fields match. A value of `$set` matches whenever the other field has any value. |

`meta` on the *type* carries `icon`, `bpmnType`, `editor`, and `roles` — capability tags (`data-element`, `signal`, `instrument`, …) that let the app find types by what they are rather than by name. Most roles are inferred from the type graph; declare one only when inference cannot see it.

## Attribute precedence

One attribute can be declared twice — on the business object (its own type, or a trait that `extends` it) and on the extension wrapper under `bpmn:extensionElements`. `resolveAttribute` in `packages/core/src/element/handle.ts` picks one, first match wins.

| # | The attribute is | Resolved on | Under which name |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | declared by the wrapper with `redefines` (or `replaces`), *and* the business object declares it too or the element carries traits | the business object | the local name after the `#` of the redefine |
| 2 | declared by the business object's own type, traits included | the business object | the declared name (`bpmn:id` and `bpmn:name` collapse to `id` and `name`) |
| 3 | declared by the wrapper | the wrapper | the declared name |
| 4 | declared by neither | the wrapper if there is one and the element carries no traits, otherwise the business object | the local name |

: Which of the two an attribute resolves on. {#tbl-attribute-precedence}

"Carries traits" is `StudyflowElement.hasTraits`: at least one attribute of the business object's own type sits in an extension namespace or carries a `redefines`. With the shipped schemas that holds for *every* element (`studyflow:BaseElement` redefines `bpmn:documentation` onto `bpmn:BaseElement`), so rule 1 needs only the wrapper's redefine and rule 4 always lands on the business object, where moddle files an undeclared name in the raw `$attrs` bag. A write resolving to no target is dropped with a console warning naming the attribute and the element.

A read that lands on the business object (rules 1 and 2) while a wrapper exists asks `extensionValueWins` whether to return the wrapper's value instead. The wrapper must hold a value at all — `undefined`, and an `isMany` property moddle initialized to `[]`, do not count — then any of these settles it.

| # | The wrapper's value wins when |
|---|---|
| 1 | the wrapper's property is `meta.pinned: true` |
| 2 | the wrapper stores the value explicitly — an own property, not a default moddle materialized on the prototype (`hasStoredValue` uses `hasOwnProperty` to tell those apart) |
| 3 | the business object does not store it explicitly either |

So a stored business-object value beats a wrapper *default*, loses to a wrapper value actually written, and loses to a pinned wrapper property even one carrying only its default. `tests/element.unit.spec.ts` pins each case by name.

### Worked example: `operationType`

`functional:Transform` declares `operationType` (`default: transform`, `meta.pinned: true`); `functional:Map` sets `default: map` and `redefines: functional:Transform#operationType`. Both are wrappers: placing either creates a `bpmn:ServiceTask` and hangs the schema type off it as an extension element.

| The element | Rule | A write goes to | A read returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bpmn:ServiceTask` + `functional:Transform` | 3 — only the wrapper declares it | the wrapper, which is where a saved file shows it: `<functional:transform operationType="…"/>` | what was written |
| `bpmn:ServiceTask` + `functional:Map` | 1 — the wrapper redefines it, and every element carries traits | the business object — and since no trait declares `operationType` on `bpmn:ServiceTask`, into its raw `$attrs` | the wrapper's pinned `map`, by exception 1 above |

: One attribute, two wrappers, two destinations. {#tbl-operation-type}

Adding `redefines` to a wrapper property does not merely rename it, it moves where the value lands; pair it with `meta.pinned: true` and the write goes somewhere the read never looks, so an edit appears to do nothing. Redefine when the BPMN side genuinely declares the attribute, the way `studyflow:Implementation` redefines `bpmn:ServiceTask#implementation` — which is why a saved file carries `implementation` on `<bpmn:serviceTask>` itself and `operationType` on the wrapper beside it.

## Function calls (`implementation` / `arguments`)

Any activity can declare the software that implements it: BPMN's own `implementation` attribute (redefined once by the core schema) carries the reference, and the core `studyflow:Arguments` trait (on every `bpmn:Activity`) carries the arguments.

| Attribute | Holds | In the BPMN XML form |
|---|---|---|
| `implementation` | A scheme-prefixed reference, `<scheme>://<ref>[@<version-or-digest>]`. The ref/version split happens at the last `@`, so docker digests parse correctly. | an attribute on the activity |
| `additionalArguments` | A `studyflow:YAMLString` holding the literal arguments — the role GitHub Actions' `with:` block plays. *Additional* by contract: the associations fill the signature first, and this supplies what is left over. Anything the step *reads* is a data association, not an entry here; a name bound by both is an error rather than a precedence question. The reserved `args` key lists positional arguments, and a nested mapping carrying its own `implementation` is a call resolved before the outer one. | a `<studyflow:additionalArguments>` child element holding the YAML as its text |

| Scheme | Names |
|---|---|
| `python://` | an importable callable, e.g. `python://sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline.fit` |
| `docker://` | an image, e.g. `docker://ghcr.io/lab/img@sha256:...` |
| `https://`, `file://` | a script URL, or a local script |
| anything else | allowed, but flagged as unresolved — a cognitive task imported from jsPsych names its plugin as `jspsych://...` |

A data association carries one expression — BPMN's own `transformation` element, used as-is, so it carries its own per-expression `language` — whose body is `slot = selection`, each half optional.

| Half | What it decides |
|---|---|
| the slot | *Which* callable parameter the value fills. Blank binds by the element's own name; `self` binds an unbound method's receiver; `*` appends positionally, the only way into `train_test_split(*arrays)`. |
| the selection | *What* value arrives, as member access and indexing (`folds['train']`). On an output association the drawn target is the slot, so the body is a selection over `result` (`result[0]`) — which is how one call fills several properties. |

Selections coordinate, they never compute: anything that calculates is a step with its own `implementation`. Saved standard XML splits the halves — the slot becomes the synthesized `DataInput`'s name, the body keeps the pure selection — and opening folds them back together.

```yaml
Fit:
  implementation: python://sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline.fit
  dataInputAssociations:
    Association_Estimator:
      transformation: self             # the receiver: bound first, positionally
      sourceRef: [Estimator]
    Association_Features:
      transformation: X
      sourceRef: [X_Train]
  additionalArguments:
    sample_weight: null         # what the associations did not supply

Score:                          # both halves in one attribute: a slice, not the whole element
  implementation: python://sklearn.metrics.accuracy_score
  dataInputAssociations:
    Association_Truth:
      transformation: y_true = folds['test']   # which slot, and what arrives there
      sourceRef: [Folds]
```

Both round-trip losslessly through the `.studyflow` YAML form, where `arguments` inlines as a nested mapping. An `implementation` value shows a function marker on the canvas.

[Execution](../run/execution.qmd#what-each-program-actually-runs) says which program calls one; `packages/runner-py/README.md` covers the Python runner, checked against `assets/examples/sklearn_pipeline.studyflow.png`.

## Templates

A top-level `templates` entry is a preset element in the palette flyouts, the command palette, and the template gallery; `object.type` names the schema or BPMN type to instantiate, plus default property values. **Parameterize, don't proliferate**: a verb that is a generic step bound to a function (extract, tokenize, fit, fMRIPrep…) ships as a template, not a new element type — which is why `ml` declares `types: []`.

```yaml
templates:
  - description: Preprocess fMRI data for a single subject (fMRIPrep in a container).
    object:
      type: functional:Map
      bpmn:name: fMRIPrep
      bpmn:documentation: Runs fMRIPrep over one subject's BIDS directory.
      icon: iconify icon-park--brain
      keywords:              # matched by the command palette's search
        - fmriprep
        - preprocessing
      implementation: docker://nipreps/fmriprep@sha256:...
      arguments: |
        output_spaces: MNI152NLin2009cAsym
```

| `object` key | What it adds |
|---|---|
| `keywords` | How a template is found by typing rather than by browsing; give each one the words a user would actually reach for. |
| `mixins` | Template-time composition of defaults from other types (`bpmn:SubProcess`), for a preset that should behave like a specialized BPMN shape without changing the underlying schema class. Reusable inheritance belongs on `types[].superClass` instead. |
| `flowElements` | Internal nodes and connections, when the template resolves to `bpmn:SubProcess` — a whole idiom (a gateway, a conditioned back-edge, an exit) stamped out in one gesture. |
| `attributes` | Promoted attributes specific to that preset. They are *not* added back onto the schema class: the modeler generates a template-scoped derived moddle type, so they persist in the saved diagram (in both serializations) without changing other templates or the base class. Undeclared scalar properties on the object are inferred onto the same derived type. |

```yaml
templates:
  - description: Retry-until-good loop, drawn.
    object:
      bpmn:name: Repeat until
      type: bpmn:SubProcess
      flowElements:
        - id: loop_start
          type: bpmn:StartEvent
          x: 140
          y: 150
        - id: loop_work
          type: bpmn:Task
          bpmn:name: Do the work
          x: 220
          y: 130
        - type: bpmn:SequenceFlow
          sourceRef: loop_start
          targetRef: loop_work

  - description: Preprocess EEG data for a single subject.
    object:
      type: functional:Map
      bpmn:name: Preprocess EEG
      mixins:
        - bpmn:SubProcess

  - description: Preprocess EEG data for a single subject.
    object:
      type: functional:Map
      bpmn:name: EEGPrep
      attributes:
        param1:
          range: string
          description: Template-specific promoted attribute.
          ifabsent: default_value
```

## Cross-schema references

Use the schema prefix: `studyflow:YAMLString`, `cognitive:AssignmentAlgorithmEnum`, `studyflow:Dataset`. That is how `eeg:Recording` extends `studyflow:Dataset`, and how the functional schema pins `functional:Transform#operationType` on subtypes like `Map`.

## Common mistakes

| Mistake | What happens |
|---|---|
| Referring to the core schema as `core` | Its `name` is Core but its prefix is `studyflow`, and every reference goes through the prefix. |
| A property with no `type` | It falls back to string-like behavior and may produce unintended interfaces. |
| `extends` where `superClass` was meant | `extends` mixes attributes onto an existing BPMN base; `superClass` defines a new concrete type. |
| Expecting a native BPMN attribute to appear | It will not, until a schema `redefines` it. |
| Inventing a tab | A category no schema declares sorts after every declared one. File the property under a declared tab instead. |
| Omitting or misconfiguring `meta.bpmnType` | The element may no longer map to the intended BPMN shape. |
| Malformed `condition.body` JSON | Conditional visibility is disabled. |
| A `redefines` with an invalid owner | It is dropped. |
| A long `description` | It renders in a tooltip. Rationale belongs in these docs or in a YAML comment. |

Property names are camelCase (`consentFormUri`, `completionCodeType`), except where a value mirrors an external tool's CLI one-to-one — the fMRIPrep template's `output_spaces` matches that flag verbatim, so configurations copy-paste.
